projects.name: Solar + Energy Storage on Garage
projects.description: Install 5-7 solar panels on south-facing garage roof face (20x12 ft, ~2-2.8 kW) plus battery storage. Solar = standalone ROI investment (~5yr payback at $0.42/kWh). Battery = generator alternative (no lot space for generator). 30% federal ITC applies to both when paired.
projects.notes: DESIGN: South garage face only. 5 portrait panels = 2.0 kW; 7 mixed = 2.8 kW. ~3,200-4,500 kWh/yr production (20-26% offset). All-in after ITC: solar ~$9-10k, battery ~$9-10k. VENDORS: Sunergy (sunergy.com) — EnergySage 2026 CA Installer of Year, Enphase Platinum, no door-to-door. NRG Clean Power (nrgcleanpower.com) — Diamond Certified, 35yr, San Mateo County, 40yr warranty. Tesla Energy (tesla.com/energy) — online only. AVOID: Sunrun.

tasks.title: Analyze energy usage and size system
tasks.notes: 17,178 kWh/yr at $0.42/kWh avg. Target: 5-7 panels south garage face (20x12 ft) = 2-2.8 kW. ~5yr payback after ITC.

tasks.title: Research and shortlist solar installers
tasks.notes: Shortlist: Sunergy (sunergy.com, Enphase Platinum, no door-to-door), NRG Clean Power (nrgcleanpower.com, Diamond Certified, San Mateo County), Tesla Energy (tesla.com/energy, online only). Avoid Sunrun.

tasks.title: Contact installers for quotes
tasks.notes: Spec: south garage face (20x12 ft, 5-7 panels, ~2-2.8 kW), paired battery (Enphase IQ or Powerwall 3), detached garage sub-panel interconnect. Ask each for: $/W, panel brand, inverter type, battery spec, warranty, timeline, ITC total. Request free shade/LIDAR analysis.

tasks.title: Compare quotes and select installer
tasks.notes: Prefer Enphase microinverters over string inverter. Compare $/W, battery spec, warranty, timeline. 30% ITC on full system incl. battery.

tasks.title: Confirm ITC timing — credit files in year PTO is granted
tasks.notes: 30% federal ITC on Form 5695. Claimed in tax year Permission to Operate granted by PG&E. Battery qualifies only when solar-paired. Plan install timing accordingly.

insights.summary: The stable 24–28 device count with zero camera motion at 11:43 PM indicates the presence metric is driven by stationary IoT network devices rather than human occupancy, which may cause unnecessary automations to trigger.

The sustained 18-20 device count paired with zero camera activity and no other evening indicators strongly suggests the presence system is counting IoT network devices rather than actual occupants. This false occupancy signal should be filtered out to prevent unnecessary automation triggers or security alerts.

The stable high presence count paired with zero camera coverage indicates a false sense of occupancy monitoring; the cameras are likely offline or in privacy mode, leaving the home unwatched during peak evening hours when the family and dogs are most active.

The persistent 18-20 device count combined with zero camera activity during typical evening hours strongly suggests a surge in non-human IoT connections rather than additional people, and verifying the camera feeds is important to ensure the home monitoring system is actually recording.

The sustained high presence count (20-26) with zero camera activity and a sudden drop to 21 at 18:32 indicates IoT device cycling or a brief network fluctuation rather than physical movement, which may temporarily affect automation reliability.

The steady rise from 17 to 24 connected devices between 4:40 PM and 5:31 PM, combined with zero camera motion events, suggests devices are stationary and likely arriving in vehicles or garages rather than moving through the house. This count significantly exceeds the household baseline and warrants monitoring for guests or unauthorized network access.

The sustained count of 17-20 connected devices during a typical Tuesday afternoon school hours suggests an unexpected schedule deviation, such as the children being home, guests visiting, or IoT devices being counted, which is worth noting for Steve.

The consistent presence of 23–26 connected devices paired with zero camera motion over four hours strongly indicates the household is in a stationary, low-activity state, likely due to family members resting or devices charging/playing media. This pattern confirms the earlier low-severity flags and suggests no immediate security concern, though a quick verification is warranted if the family expected to be active.

The sustained presence of 21–26 mobile devices paired with zero camera motion over four hours strongly indicates a large, stationary gathering (likely guests over for dinner or a movie night) rather than normal household activity. This pattern suggests routine social hosting, but warrants attention for security zoning and energy management.

The persistent 21–23 connected devices paired with zero camera motion over four hours suggests either the house is unoccupied with devices left on standby, or the household is entirely confined to a camera-blind zone. A quick verification of camera status and a routine check would rule out sensor failure or an unattended area.
